structured.answer: Not for me: it's American shares in English and letters, it fell 4.82% in one day and once lost a third (-33.71%), so I'm keeping my deposits. If anything, I'll ask my son or the bank.

stuck.why: Didn't know what to choose since I'm not in Europe; pressed Save without understanding
Name and labels all English abbreviations (ETF, UCITS, Acc, TER); couldn't tell if it was anything like saving

used: Title 'iShares Core S&P 500 UCITS ETF USD (Acc)'
Yellow warning 'may not be eligible for acquisition in your country of residence'
Chart headline '1 year: +13.79%' and red part below zero
Maximum drawdown rows, esp. '-33.71%' since inception
skipped: Basics, Holdings, Performance, Stock exchange sections
not_found: Any plain sentence on whether it is safe compared with a deposit
Anything in Hebrew or about Israel
What it costs me in shekels

findings.what: Large red '-35.72 | -4.82%' daily change is the first number you see, which frightened me off at once
Whole page in English and abbreviations; no plain explanation for an ordinary saver
Warning that the product may not be eligible in my country, so I didn't know if I could buy it at all
Column of minus figures (-22.60%, -33.71%) with no sentence saying what it means for my money
Chart's grey axis numbers too small and pale to read
Settings pop-up blocks the page at the start and asks for a country without Israel shown
